title: Waymo starts driverless rides in Detroit; public service planned
key_facts: Waymo began fully autonomous (no human driver) driving in Detroit on Tuesday 6 Oct 2026.
Rides are limited to Waymo employees while it builds a safety framework for the city.
Waymo plans public riders in the near future once the technology is properly validated.
It will drive in downtown, Corktown, Midtown, Hamtramck and Indian Village, then expand across the metro area over time.
The step follows several months of familiarising the Waymo Driver with the city and working with local officials.
quote_evidence: The service will only be available to Waymo employees while it establishes a “safety framework” for operating in the city, the company says.
Though the service isn’t open to public riders quite yet, the announcement marks a major step toward Waymo’s eventual expansion across the Metro Detroit area.
why_it_matters_hint: Detroit is another city moving from supervised testing to driverless cars, with public rides still to come.
